items.title: Edmond "Doc" Souchon Interview, 1962-02-17
items.q: felt his oats very much was Baby Todd's when he was in Chicago

ctx.x: That is the closest thing to the old type of music that Bud... That Oliver played in those days. Yes, yes. They were dressed up and they were big shots and all that. And the attitude was very nice. I mean, the one that was pretty much of a... felt his oats very much was Baby Todd's when he was in Chicago. But Oliver was just as cordial and nice as he could be. Well, when the 30s, I mean in the 40s, the middle 40s, early 40s came along, a chap by the name of Scoop Kennedy, who is now connected with WDSU-TV, he's an authority on cooking. He was a guiding light in the formation of the National Jazz Foundation, which promised to be a very great thing. And we had chapters all over the world, and it was a little Mimicraft magazine that didn't amount to too much. His secretary put it out.
